findings.evidence: Mathlib/Algebra/Algebra/Basic.lean:169 `abbrev semiringToRing (R) [CommRing R] ... := { __ := Module.addCommMonoidToAddCommGroup R, ... }` with `See note [reducible non-instances]`. The letI is forced only because `Module.Free k H` over a field needs `AddCommGroup H`; every Mathlib API actually used is already stated more generally — `TensorProduct.dualDistribEquiv` (Contraction.lean:462) needs `[CommSemiring R] [AddCommMonoid M] [Module.Finite] [Module.Free]`, `Module.evalEquiv` (Dual/Defs.lean:229) needs `[CommSemiring R] [AddCommMonoid M] [IsReflexive]`, and `Module.Finite.linearMap`/`Module.Free.linearMap` (FreeModule/Finite/Matrix.lean:44,47) need `[Ring R] [AddCommGroup M]` — i.e. the weakening moves away from, not toward, the reusable API.
findings.fix: Restore `[AddCommGroup H]`/`[Ring H]` (and `FiniteDimensional k H`, which is an abbrev for `Module.Finite`), deleting all eight `letI`/`let _` lines. If generalization is the goal, the axis with actual payoff is the base ring: `[CommRing k] [AddCommGroup H] [Module k H] [Module.Finite k H] [Module.Free k H]`.
findings.issue: The weakening of the section variables to `[AddCommMonoid H]`/`[Semiring H]` (Basic.lean:68, 95, 295, 370, 411) admits no new examples: over a `Field k`, every `Module k H` is uniquely an `AddCommGroup` and every `Algebra k H` a `Ring`. The file proves this itself by rebuilding the discarded structure at eight sites — Basic.lean:63, 80, 88, 136, 145 (`Module.addCommMonoidToAddCommGroup k`) and Functoriality.lean:182, 191, 231 (`Algebra.semiringToRing k`). Both are `reducible non-instances` in Mathlib precisely because they create diamonds: the reconstructed `Neg` is `fun x => (-1 : k) • x`, not defeq to a user's own `AddCommGroup H`, so `dualDistribEquiv` and `evalLinearEquiv` unfold to Mathlib's `TensorProduct.dualDistribEquiv`/`Module.evalEquiv` at an instance a downstream user cannot match syntactically.

findings.evidence: Basic.lean:427-445 `ofConv_mul_apply (w) (x) : (LinearMap.mul' k (ConvolutionDual k H) w).ofConv x = dualDistribEquiv k H w (Coalgebra.comul x)`; its proof cites only `LinearMap.mul'_apply`, `LinearMap.convMul_apply`, `dualDistribEquiv_tmul_apply`, none of which mention `HopfAlgebra.antipode`.
findings.fix: Move `ofConv_mul_apply` into the Bialgebra section (Basic.lean:295, hypotheses `[Semiring H] [Bialgebra k H] [Module.Finite k H]`), drop `private`, and delete `convMul_apply_eq_dualDistribEquiv`, replacing its uses by `ofConv_mul_apply k H (phi ⊗ₜ psi) x` (with `LinearMap.mul'_apply`).
findings.issue: `convMul_apply_eq_dualDistribEquiv` re-proves the pure-tensor special case of `ConvolutionDual.ofConv_mul_apply` (Basic.lean:427), which states the same fact for arbitrary `w : CD ⊗ CD`. That general lemma is unusable here only because it is `private` and sits in the `HopfAlgebra` section (Basic.lean:411) although its statement and proof use no antipode — only `LinearMap.convMul_apply` and `dualDistribEquiv_tmul_apply`.

findings.evidence: Both blocks reduce on pure tensors to `phi.ofConv x * psi.ofConv y` via `evalAlgHom_apply_apply`; lines 219-224 and 254-259 are the same `TensorProduct.induction_on` skeleton with the roles of the two arguments swapped.

findings.issue: The inline induction in `evalAlgHom.map_mul'` (215-224) and `dualDistribEquiv_tensor_eval_apply` (247-259) are two special cases of one biadditive statement, proved separately by the same tensor induction.

findings.evidence: Line 82 `exact LinearMap.convMul_comp_coalgHom_distrib phi psi f.toCoalgHom`; Mathlib/RingTheory/Coalgebra/Convolution.lean:124 gives that lemma for `h : B →ₗc[R] C` with only `[AddCommMonoid B] [Module R B] [CoalgebraStruct R B]`, and the convolution algebra `WithConv (C →ₗ[R] A)` (Convolution.lean:187) requires no finiteness.
findings.fix: State them for `f : H →ₗc[k] K` with `[AddCommMonoid H] [Module k H] [Coalgebra k H]` (same for `K`) and no `Module.Finite`, and state `dualDistribEquiv_tensor_map_apply` for `TensorProduct.map (mapLinear k f) (mapLinear k f)`; `map` then only adds the comultiplication half, which is where `Bialgebra` and finiteness are genuinely used.
findings.issue: `mapLinear` (56), `mapAlgHom` (67) and `dualDistribEquiv_tensor_map_apply` (92) take a `BialgHom` and carry `[Semiring H] [Bialgebra k H]`/`[Semiring K] [Bialgebra k K]`, but use only coalgebra data: `map_mul'` (82) uses `f.toCoalgHom`, `map_one'`/`commutes'` use only the counit, and no finiteness is needed. The algebra structures on `H` and `K` and the algebra half of `f` are unused.

summary: The PR-wide typeclass weakening (AddCommGroup→AddCommMonoid, Ring→Semiring) buys no new examples over a field and is paid for by eight `letI` reconstructions of the discarded structure via Mathlib's diamond-prone reducible non-instances. Three convolution/dualDistrib facts are also proved as special cases of results the PR already has or could state once in general.
